messages.subject: Compiling from Source Question
parts:
Hello:

I am compiling from source because I need to create a renjin jar without dependencies included.  I am getting a conflict with guava and I suspect others will follow.

If there is an easier way to get a jar without dependencies, this please let me know! :)


My issue:
I cannot get the following command to run successfully:

vagrant ssh -c "cd renjin && mvn clean install"


I downloaded master branch and I've run "vagrant up" successfully.

I examined the VM and the renjin directory exists and mirrors my local machine as expected.  However when the command, I get the test failure shown below in BOLD.


Do you have any suggestions?  I tried this several times from scratch and it always fails at this point.


Environment:

  • Virtual Box: v. 5/0/14 [Box 'ubuntu/trusty32' (v20160122.0.0)]
  • OS X El Capitan: 10.11.2
  • Java Version (OS X): 1.8.0_71
  • Java Version (Virtual Box): 1.8.0_72


Thanks any help.

Kevin Beatty

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Compiling from Source Question
parts:
Hi Kevin,
You can find binaries (without dependencies) for all Renjin artifacts
and releases here:
https://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/org/renjin/

If you have a maven/gradle/ivy/sbt/ build etc, you should just be able
to include renjin-script-engine in your build:

<dependency>
<groupId>org.renjin</groupId>
<artifactId>renjin-script-engine</artifactId>
<version>RELEASE</version>
</dependency>

Depending on your build tool, you should be able to excerise some
control over transitive dependency conflict resolution such as Guava,
though Renjin won't run against earlier versions of Guava.

We have an open request to repackage Guava in Renjin's namespace to
avoid these problems:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/63

I'll also take a look at the Vagrant setup to see why the build is
failing there...

Alex
